n714c367faf4.s: Kesavananda Bharati (24 April 1973) was decided by a 13-judge bench by what majority?
n714c367faf4.x: Kesavananda Bharati was decided on 24 April 1973 by a 13-judge bench with a 7:6 majority.

n923d3a8172f.s: Under the present position, Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights under Article 368:
o: Provided the basic structure is not damaged
Only outside the scope of Article 368
n923d3a8172f.x: Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights under Article 368, but the amendment remains subject to the basic structure limitation.

naa1772d1671.s: The criticism of the basic structure doctrine as 'judicial rewriting' of the Constitution rests mainly on its:
o: Absence of any explicit textual definition
naa1772d1671.x: The doctrine has no explicit textual definition and its content is developed by unelected judges case by case, which is the basis of the criticism.

n2aea429a74b.s: Which former CJI told the JPC that the 129th Amendment Bill, 2024, did not violate the basic structure?
n2aea429a74b.x: B.R. Gavai said the Bill did not violate the basic structure, whereas U.U. Lalit and Sanjiv Khanna raised doubts.

nindian-polity-38-15.s: Which of the following cannot be done even through an amendment under Article 368?
o: Placing a law in the Ninth Schedule
nindian-polity-38-15.x: The basic structure cannot be destroyed even under Article 368; Fundamental Rights and the Preamble remain amendable subject to it.

n8de89b726e0.s: The present position on the Preamble is that it is:
o: Not a part of the Constitution
Part of the Constitution but not amendable at all
The sole content of the basic structure
Part of the Constitution and amendable, subject to the basic structure
n8de89b726e0.x: The Preamble is part of the Constitution and amendable subject to the basic structure, which is not confined to the Preamble.

ned440a9f440.s: Secularism was treated as a basic feature of the Constitution:
o: Only after the 42nd Amendment added 'secular' to the Preamble
Even before the 42nd Amendment added 'secular' to the Preamble
Only because of its textual insertion in 1976
ned440a9f440.x: Secularism was treated as a basic feature even before the 42nd Amendment (1976) added the word 'secular' to the Preamble.

nindian-polity-41-21.s: In which case were free and fair elections held part of the basic structure while parts of the 39th Amendment were struck down?
o: Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain
nindian-polity-41-21.x: In striking down parts of the 39th Amendment (Article 329A), Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain held free and fair elections to be part of the basic structure.

n5cdaa36490d.s: Recognition of secularism as a basic feature is associated with which case?
n5cdaa36490d.x: S.R. Bommai recognised secularism as a basic feature; Indra Sawhney dealt with the creamy layer, the 50 per cent ceiling and promotions.

ncfc3748d4b0.s: The Vishaka guidelines on sexual harassment at the workplace were later replaced by:
o: The Representation of the People Act
ncfc3748d4b0.x: The Vishaka guidelines on workplace sexual harassment were later replaced by the POSH Act, 2013.

nindian-polity-24-27.s: Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillu upheld the constitutional validity of which Schedule?
nindian-polity-24-27.x: Kihoto Hollohan upheld the anti-defection law in the Tenth Schedule and held the Speaker's decisions under it open to judicial review.

nindian-polity-24-46.s: Minerva Mills v. Union of India is linked to which Constitutional Amendment?
nindian-polity-24-46.x: Minerva Mills is linked to the 42nd Amendment; the 39th is linked to Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain.

nindian-polity-41-9.s: Champakam Dorairajan led to the First Amendment inserting which Article?
nindian-polity-41-9.x: Champakam Dorairajan led to the First Amendment, which inserted Article 15(4).

n38baa777575.s: Navtej Singh Johar (2018), which read down Section 377 IPC, was delivered by a Bench of:
n38baa777575.x: A five-judge Bench in Navtej Singh Johar read down Section 377 and decriminalised consensual same-sex acts between adults.

n6e93e615dd5.s: The Anoop Baranwal (2023) committee of the PM, LoP and CJI for selecting Election Commissioners was to operate:
o: Only till Parliament made a law
Only until the next CJI took office
n6e93e615dd5.x: The Court's committee was to operate only until Parliament made a law, which Parliament did in 2023.

n2e6285961f8.s: Which 2013 Supreme Court judgment led to the NOTA option on EVMs?
n2e6285961f8.x: PUCL (2013) brought the NOTA option; Lily Thomas (2013) struck down Section 8(4) of the Representation of the People Act.

n705c8b5df3c.s: Amaravati became the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh with effect from:
n705c8b5df3c.x: After the High Court's 2022 ruling against three capitals, Amaravati became the sole capital from 2 June 2024.

n4004caf1cac.s: Under the Aadhaar judgment (2018), authentication records may be retained for a maximum of:
n4004caf1cac.x: The limit is six months; three months is the common trap.

nd8a3392a1be.s: Vishaka was decided by a three-judge Bench headed by:
nd8a3392a1be.x: Vishaka was decided by a three-judge Bench headed by CJI J.S. Verma.

n1caa09903f5.s: In State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara (1951), the Prohibition Act was:
o: Struck down because it touched imports
Upheld as a public-health measure though it incidentally touched imports
Upheld on the ground of territorial nexus
n1caa09903f5.x: Applying pith and substance, the Court upheld the Prohibition Act as a public-health measure even though it incidentally touched imports.

n741df9ff0b4.s: State of Bombay v. R.M.D.C. (1957), on taxing prize competitions run from outside the State, is associated with:
n741df9ff0b4.x: Taxing prize competitions run from outside the State needed a nexus with the State, so the case is associated with territorial nexus.

n61de894fc19.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about determining the true character of a law?
o: Its object and effect are considered
A.S. Krishna (1957) is associated with this approach
Only the title given to the legislation is examined
n61de894fc19.x: The true character is not judged merely by the title; the whole Act, its object and its effect are considered.

n57ee9777a68.s: Which of the following pairs (doctrine – foreign origin) is correctly matched?
n57ee9777a68.x: 'Procedure established by law' comes from Japan; prospective overruling is from the USA, the pleasure doctrine from England and separation of powers from Montesquieu (France).

n807374e3744.s: In Indian constitutional law, the doctrine of separation of powers is:
o: Applicable only to the executive and judiciary
n807374e3744.x: Indian separation of powers is functional rather than rigid (Ram Jawaya Kapur, 1955) and is part of the basic structure (Kesavananda Bharati).

new.s: The idea of implied limits on the amending power was drawn from the Basic Law of which country?
new.x: Dietrich Conrad drew on Germany's Basic Law in arguing for implied limitations in 1965.

new.s: Who headed the 13-judge bench in Kesavananda Bharati?
new.x: CJI S.M. Sikri headed the 13-judge bench; Mudholkar dissented in Sajjan Singh and Conrad was a German jurist.

new.s: Which case FIRST limited Parliament's power to amend Fundamental Rights?
new.x: Golaknath (1967) first limited the power to amend FRs; Kesavananda Bharati (1973) first propounded the basic structure doctrine.

new.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Golaknath
2. Kesavananda Bharati
3. Shankari Prasad
4. Minerva Mills
new.x: Shankari Prasad (1951), Golaknath (1967), Kesavananda Bharati (1973), Minerva Mills (1980).

new.s: Golaknath (1967) was decided by a bench of:
new.x: Golaknath was decided by 11 judges by a 6:5 majority; Kesavananda had 13 judges, 7:6.

new.s: In Shankari Prasad (1951), the Supreme Court held that a constitutional amendment is:
o: Void if it touches Fundamental Rights
new.x: Shankari Prasad held that Art. 368 covers FRs and an amendment is not 'law' under Art. 13; Golaknath later held the opposite.

new.s: Which Constitutional Amendment was challenged in Golaknath (1967)?
new.x: Golaknath challenged the 17th Amendment; the 24th (1971) was Parliament's reply to Golaknath.

new.s: The 39th Amendment clause, Article 329A(4), was struck down in:
o: Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain
new.x: Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975) struck down the 39th Amendment clause that put the PM's election disputes beyond courts.

new.s: Kesavananda Bharati upheld which Amendment that had amended Articles 13 and 368?
new.x: The 24th Amendment (1971) amended Arts. 13 and 368 and was upheld in Kesavananda Bharati.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Amendment – case) is correctly matched?
o: 42nd Amendment – Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain
new.x: The 99th Amendment (NJAC) was struck down in the SC Advocates-on-Record case (2015); the 39th fell in Raj Narain and the 42nd in Minerva Mills.

new.s: The principle of equality was declared a basic feature in which case?
new.x: Indra Sawhney (1992) is associated with the principle of equality as a basic feature.

new.s: The Supreme Court's powers under Articles 32, 136, 141 and 142 were held basic in which case?
new.x: Delhi Judicial Service Association (1991) is linked to the SC's powers under Arts. 32, 136, 141, 142; L. Chandra Kumar concerns HC powers under Arts. 226, 227.

new.s: Article 31C was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
new.x: Art. 31C came by the 25th Amendment (1971), not the First; the 42nd only widened it.

new.s: How many Acts did the Ninth Schedule contain at the start?
new.x: The Ninth Schedule began with 13 Acts; it now has 282.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about I.R. Coelho (2007):
1. It was decided by a nine-judge bench.
2. It gave blanket immunity to all Ninth Schedule laws.
3. Its test looks at the essence of Articles 14, 19 and 21.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Coelho (nine judges) denied blanket immunity and applied the rights test based on Arts. 14, 19, 21, so statement 2 is wrong.

new.s: Which of the following originated with Parliament rather than the Supreme Court?
new.x: Art. 13(4) came from Parliament through the 24th Amendment; the other three are Supreme Court doctrines.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a doctrine evolved by the Supreme Court?
o: DPSP primacy over Articles 14 and 19 under Article 31C
new.x: DPSP primacy under Art. 31C came from Parliament through the 25th Amendment (1971); the rest are Supreme Court doctrines.

new.s: The precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle were laid down in:
new.x: Vellore Citizens (1996) laid down the precautionary and polluter pays principles.

new.s: The doctrine of public trust is associated with which case?
new.x: The public trust doctrine is associated with Kamal Nath (1997).

new.s: The principle of absolute liability was evolved in:
new.x: Absolute liability came from the Oleum gas case (1987).

new.s: Which of the following pairs (doctrine – case) is correctly matched?
new.x: Colourable legislation is linked to Gajapati Narayan Deo (1953); eclipse is Bhikaji Narain, public trust Kamal Nath, absolute liability the Oleum gas case.

new.s: The doctrine of eclipse is associated with which case?
new.x: The doctrine of eclipse is associated with Bhikaji Narain (1955).

new.s: T.N. Godavarman (1996) is known as the:
new.x: T.N. Godavarman (1996) is the forest case.

new.s: Rameshwar Prasad (2006) declared which action void?
o: The dissolution of the Bihar Assembly
new.x: Rameshwar Prasad (2006) held the dissolution of the Bihar Assembly void.

new.s: Which case held that the Governor acts on advice?
new.x: Nabam Rebia (2016) held that the Governor acts on advice.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Governor's role in assent:
1. State of Tamil Nadu v Governor (April 2025) is linked to deemed assent.
2. The Presidential reference opinion of November 2025 fixed timelines for assent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The April 2025 TN case is linked to deemed assent, but the November 2025 Presidential reference said no timelines.

new.s: S.R. Bommai (1994) was decided by a Bench of:
new.x: S.R. Bommai was decided by nine judges.

new.s: Instant triple talaq is punishable with up to how many years' imprisonment under the 2019 Act passed after Shayara Bano?
new.x: Following Shayara Bano (2017), the 2019 Act made instant triple talaq punishable with up to 3 years.

new.s: Shayara Bano (2017) declared instant triple talaq void by what majority?
new.x: Shayara Bano was decided 3:2; 6:1 is Davinder Singh.

new.s: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024) overruled which case on the Andhra Pradesh Act, 2000?
new.x: Davinder Singh allowed SC sub-classification and overruled E.V. Chinnaiah (2004), which concerned the AP Act of 2000.

new.s: Davinder Singh (2024) on sub-classification of SCs was decided by seven judges by a majority of:
new.x: Davinder Singh was decided by seven judges, 6:1.

new.s: Guidelines on the arrest memo were laid down in:
new.x: D.K. Basu (1997) laid down the arrest memo guidelines; Prem Shankar Shukla concerns handcuffing.

new.s: Police reforms are associated with which case?
new.x: Prakash Singh is the police reforms case; Lalita Kumari concerns mandatory FIRs.

new.s: The Aadhaar scheme was upheld in 2018 by what majority?
new.x: The Aadhaar judgment upheld the scheme 4:1.

new.s: The December 2023 Article 370 judgment was delivered by a Bench headed by:
new.x: The Article 370 and Electoral Bonds benches were headed by CJI Chandrachud.

new.s: The doctrine of parens patriae treats the State as:
o: The legal protector of citizens unable to protect themselves
The final interpreter of the Constitution
A party bound by its own previous decisions
new.x: Parens patriae treats the State as the legal protector of citizens who cannot protect themselves.

new.s: The doctrine of territorial nexus relates to:
new.x: Territorial nexus upholds a State law operating outside the State if there is a sufficient nexus.

new.s: The doctrine of colourable legislation tests the legislature's:
new.x: Colourable legislation tests competence, not motive: what cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly.

new.s: The leading case on the doctrine of colourable legislation is:
new.x: K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo (1953) is the leading case on colourable legislation.

new.s: Under the doctrine of eclipse, a pre-Constitution law conflicting with Fundamental Rights is:
new.x: Eclipse holds that such a law is overshadowed, not void (Bhikaji Narain, 1955).

new.s: Which case held that Fundamental Rights cannot be waived?
new.x: Basheshar Nath (1959) held that FRs cannot be waived.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a federal interpretation doctrine?
new.x: Eclipse is an FR doctrine under Art. 13; the others are federal doctrines.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Fundamental Rights doctrines:
1. Under severability, only the invalid part of a law goes if the rest is complete.
2. Fundamental Rights can be waived by the person concerned.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Severability removes only the invalid part; FRs cannot be waived (Basheshar Nath, 1959).

new.s: Article 254(2) applies to repugnancy in matters of which List?
new.x: Only Concurrent List matters attract Art. 254(2); in the State List the State law prevails in its field.

new.s: Under Article 254(2), a State law reserved for and assented to by the President:
o: Prevails in that State, but Parliament may later override it
Prevails permanently over any law of Parliament
Is void if repugnant to a Central law
Applies to the whole of India
new.x: A State law with President's assent prevails in that State, but Parliament may later override it.

new.s: Which 2018 judgment relied on transformative constitutionalism only?
new.x: Joseph Shine used transformative constitutionalism only; NCT Delhi used constitutional morality only; Navtej and Sabarimala used both.

new.s: Which 2018 case relied on constitutional morality only?
new.x: NCT Delhi used constitutional morality only, while Navtej Johar and Sabarimala used both doctrines.

new.s: The doctrine of pith and substance originated in:
new.x: Pith and substance came from Canada, not the USA.

new.s: The doctrine of public trust originated in:
new.x: The public trust doctrine traces to Roman law.
